finish_qa.method: finish_frames hibit v1 (the hi-bit studio recipe, forge_hibit): the hd registration; one palette per character (given, or k-means++ on luminance-weighted RGB of up to 200000 opaque source pixels, 16 colours by default); every sub-pixel of an 8x8 supersampled box downscale takes its nearest palette colour and every output pixel the colour covering most of its cell (a majority vote, never a blend; under 45% coverage transparent; the previous frame's colour kept while it holds 80% of the winner, an opaque cell kept down to 33%); forge_palette.quantize_sequence and cleanup_alpha; forge_hibit.clean_isolated (a lone pixel takes its 4-neighbours' majority unless 90 apart in luminance-weighted RGB, so eyes and glints stay; 1 px islands dropped), 2 passes; a 1 px outline outside the 4-connected silhouette in a colour taken from the image (auto: the dominant saturated hue, OKLab L 0.22), a given #RRGGBB, the palette's dark shade (selective) or its darkest colour (dark); the target height includes the outline; no lift, no dither, binary alpha; flicker counted against the smooth box frames, held vs the same majority without hysteresis
notProven: identity, pose and readability at the finished size (look at review-contact.png and the frames)
that the target height suits the game camera and the rest of the cast (run lineup)
loop seams and timing (gait_loop, retime); finished frames keep the source names
hysteresis follows file order: the seam pair of a loop window chosen later is not held
the palette's fit to the character's other clips (finish them with --palette and this clip's palette.json)
that the outline colour reads against the game's backgrounds (auto takes it from the sprite)
